answer: Publicly verifiable randomness from threshold signatures lets anyone check that a random value was fairly produced, and the trellis of the design is that the value is a signature on a public seed. The thread of the protocol is that verification needs only the public key, so no trusted party is required to believe the result. A Sybil cannot forge the randomness because forging needs a threshold of signers, and the quartz of the signature proves the value came from a real quorum.
